previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with hypogammaglobulinemia, mitochondrial myopathy, coronary artery disease, and orthostatic hypotension was admitted for scheduled inpatient IVIG infusion. He received premedication with IV fluids and Benadryl, and the infusion was administered slowly overnight due to his fluid sensitivity. During the infusion, he experienced mild chest discomfort and shortness of breath, which resolved with oxygen and rate reduction. He remained on telemetry and was observed overnight. The following day, he reported residual grogginess but improved mental clarity by afternoon. He was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments, including a switch to chewable aspirin, and plans for potential transition to outpatient IVIG. No acute complications occurred.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old gentleman with ___ CAD s/p MI with 7 
angioplasties and 5 stents, HTN, HLD, mitochondrial disease, 
admitted with intermittent episodes of chest pressure, with no 
EKG changes and three negative sets of cardiac enzymes.

ACUTE ISSUES:
# Chest Pain: Episodes of pain seemed suspicious for ACS, given 
quality and duration of pain, as well as accompanying symptoms, 
with extensive past cardiac history.  Patient had no EKG changes 
with three sets of negative cardiac enzymes.  Patient had a 
normal exercise stress test, with Echo that ruled out evidence 
of ischemia.  It is possible that the patient is having anginal 
symptoms, compounded by anxiety.  Pulmonary etiology was less 
likely given lack of cough/fevers/chills/pleuritic pain, as well 
as lack of effusion/consolidation on chest x-ray.  No GI 
symptoms that would suggest GERD or PUD as a cause.  On review 
of past admissions and discussion with his PCP, it appears that 
the patient tends to develop more angina when he is dehydrated, 
in conjunction with his mitochondrial disease.  During this 
admission, the patient was treated with 2L IV normal saline.  
Additionally, he was restarted on his Plavix and provided 
morphine as needed for chest pain.  He will follow closely with 
his PCP and his cardiologist.  His aspirin, metoprolol, 
ranolazine, ___ and statin were also continued.
